requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: vgcreate/lvcreate/mkfs.ext4/mount sequence created /dev/mapper/vgdata-lvdata and mounted it at /srv/data (1.1G initial size), confirmed via df -h output showing the mount.

requirements.requirement: Grow the volume to at least 2 GB while it stays mounted
requirements.summary: A second loop-backed PV was added, vgextend + lvextend +100%FREE + online resize2fs were run while /srv/data remained mounted throughout (mount confirmed unchanged before/after), growing the LV to <2.34 GiB, well above the 2GB requirement.

requirements.requirement: Contents stay intact through the resize
requirements.summary: Test files (50MB random file + text file) were written and sha256-recorded before the extend, then verified with sha256sum -c immediately after the online resize, reporting OK for both files.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied: node1 has an LVM logical volume mounted at /srv/data, it was grown online from ~1.17GiB to ~2.34GiB while remaining mounted, and sha256 checksums confirm the existing data was untouched throughout. The executor also independently completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol (pre-restart boot_id and healthy state, reboot, confirmed disconnection/reconnection, changed boot_id matching the global after_executor snapshot, and post-restart recovery of loop devices, LVM activation, mount, and data integrity) with no contradictions against the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: No spare block device existed on node1's disk, so the LVM PVs were built on loop devices backed by sparse files rather than a real second disk/partition; this is a reasonable workaround but differs from a typical physical-device LVM setup.
The restart protocol, while thorough and internally consistent, was not part of the public task contract, so its quality does not affect the scored requirements above.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were all purposeful: package install, sparse-file/loop device creation (a legitimate workaround since vda had no spare space), PV/VG/LV creation and extension, test-data writes for the intactness proof, OpenRC persistence scripts (/etc/local.d/lvm-loop.start, rc-update add local/lvm) needed to support the mandated node-restart protocol, and the reboot itself for that protocol. No troubleshooting dead-ends, failed services, or unsafe exposure were observed; listening-socket differences before/after are just DHCP-assigned IP/PID changes from the reboot, not new exposure. Minor residue: two small files (/tmp/pre_extend.sha256, /tmp/reboot.log) were left in /tmp after the run, a low-severity, bounded leftover.
